title: Best way to run local HTML games on iPhone with sound and P2P multiplayer?
author: Fallout_Lord
selftext:
I’ve been building browser games with ChatGPT and Claude, and I’m trying to find a reliable way for friends with iPhones to play them.

My current example is a golf game contained in one HTML file, including its JavaScript, CSS and assets. It already has mobile controls and peer-to-peer multiplayer. Each person runs their own copy, and one player hosts the lobby.      
I want to share the file without setting up public web hosting. Opening local HTML through the usual iOS file previews has been the problem.

Some options I’ve come across are:      
\- Sitecase      
\- Textastic      
\- OpenHTML

I’d also love suggestions for other apps or approaches that let everyone run their own local copy.

Has anyone used these or another solution for HTML games, especially ones made with AI? I’m interested in whether sound effects, music, graphics, touch controls and P2P multiplayer work reliably during actual play.

Single-file games are my priority, but support for projects with separate scripts, images and audio files would be a bonus. Experiences with other interactive HTML apps and tools would also be helpful.

What would you recommend, what does it cost, and have you encountered issues after iOS updates?

comments.body:
